study.title: Acts 2 - The outpouring of the Spirit, the preaching of Peter and the visible birth of the church
study.overview: Acts 2 describes the public coming of the Holy Spirit upon the disciples on the day of Pentecost, the astonishment of the multitudes gathered in Jerusalem, and Peter's first great apostolic preaching. The chapter shows that the Spirit empowers the testimony, confirms Jesus as the risen and exalted Christ, calls to repentance and brings together a new community marked by teaching, communion, prayer, sharing and praise. The outcome presents the church growing daily by the action of the Lord, not just by human effort.

outline.title: The Spirit Comes and the People Reacts
outline.explanation: At Pentecost, the disciples are gathered together and the Holy Spirit descends with audible and visible signs. The immediate result is empowerment to speak in other languages, so that Jews from different regions hear the greatness of God in their own languages. The reaction is double: admiration and confusion in some, irony in others.

outline.title: Peter interprets the sign and announces Jesus
outline.explanation: Peter responds that the phenomenon is not drunkenness, but the fulfillment of Joel's prophecy about the outpoken of the Spirit in the last days. Then he centers the message in Jesus: approved by God, delivered according to the divine purpose, crucified by perverse hands, risen, exalted at the right hand of God and constituted Lord and Christ.

outline.title: Repentance, community and church growth
outline.explanation: Preaching reaches the hearts of the listeners, who ask what to do. Peter calls for repentance and baptism in the name of Jesus Christ, with a promise of forgiveness and the gift of the Spirit. Those who receive the word persevere in doctrine, in communion, in the breaking of bread and in prayers; the common life is expressed in generosity, joy, fear of God, and daily growth given by the Lord.

study.context: The chapter is located on the Jewish feast of Pentecost, when there was a great concentration of Jews and proselytes in Jerusalem. The notes highlight that this was a period of pilgrimage and that the meeting of the disciples in prayer precedes the descent of the Spirit. Peter's speech also relies on texts from the Old Testament, especially Joel's prophecy and the psalms attributed to David, showing continuity between Israel's hope and the Christian proclamation of Jesus.
study.theology: Chapter theology is Christocentric and pneumatological. The Holy Spirit does not appear as a private experience, but as a power of testimony and sign of the new phase of the history of redemption. The outpouring of the Spirit fulfills God's promise and inaugurates a community in which men and women, young and old, servants and servants participate in the divine work. The apostolic message affirms God's sovereignty over the cross, without diminishing human guilt for the rejection of Jesus. The resurrection and exaltation of Christ are the center of faith and preaching. The call to repentance, baptism, and reception of forgiveness shows that salvation involves a personal response to the announced word. The church, in turn, is born as a persevering people in teaching, communion, supper, prayer, generosity, praise and growth granted by the Lord.

scholarViews.insight: The outpouring of the Spirit at Pentecost is presented as the fulfillment of Jesus" promise to empower witnesses, and tongues serve to communicate God's works to people of various nations.
Peter preaches with power because the Spirit also acts on the listeners, producing deep conviction and leading many to the obedience of faith.
The expression "in the last days" is understood as the Messianic era, and the outpouring of the Spirit on "all flesh" highlights the expansion of the prophetic action for the people of God.

questions: How does the descent of the Spirit in Acts 2 correct the idea that the Christian faith is only human effort or religious emotion?
What does it mean, in practice, to repent and be baptized in the name of Jesus Christ as an answer to the gospel?
What characteristics of the first Christian community should mark the church today: teaching, communion, prayer, generosity and praise?
study.practice: This chapter calls the church to depend on the Holy Spirit to witness with clarity, courage and fidelity. It also confronts the reader with the need to respond to the gospel with real repentance and obedient faith in Jesus as Lord and Christ. In practice, this includes persevering in biblical doctrine, cultivating concrete communion, maintaining regular life of prayer, participating in supper with reverence, sharing resources with the needy, and living so that praise to God and witness to people walk together.
study.uncertainty: The given notes do not allow to accurately determine all the details of the phenomenon of languages or solve how to harmonize all confessional readings about baptism and the gift of the Spirit; therefore, the study describes these points as textual interpretations and not as mandatory dogmatic conclusions. There is also no basis, in the notes, to affirm additional historical data on Jerusalem beyond the context of the Feast of Pentecost and the presence of Jews and proselytes.
